title: gate-secrets.json (FLEET_OPS_REPO)
description: #1346: the gate-scoped-secrets allowlist. Lives ONLY in the operator's private OPS repo (FLEET_OPS_REPO, see src/ops-repo.ts), at the path secrets-config.ts's GATE_SECRETS_ALLOWLIST_PATH names ('gate-secrets.json'). Never in a gated repo's own fleet.json -- a PR author can edit that file, so an allowlist living there could grant itself a secret. The one top-level key that is NOT a repo slug is 'trustOwnApp' (#1380, below); every other top-level key is 'owner/repo' (matched case-insensitively, and always contains '/', which 'trustOwnApp' never does). Each repo value maps a leg name (the same string the repo's own fleet.json gate block names in its 'legs' array) to that leg's grant, in EITHER of two forms (#1376): a plain array of secret NAMEs (back-compat, equivalent to {secrets: [...]} with no head opt-in), or an object {secrets, head?}. A name is an opaque label -- never a value, an env var name, or a Worker secret binding name; secrets-registry.ts (committed, public) is the only place a name resolves to anything real, and only a TRUSTED PR (same-repo, base == the repo's own default branch, AND EITHER author_association OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR and not a bot, OR (#1380) a bot login matching THIS fleet's own GitHub App, when 'trustOwnApp' opts that in) ever receives a grant at all -- see docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-26-gate-scoped-secrets-design.md.

trustOwnApp.description: #1380 security review r1 MED: fleet-wide (never per-repo) boolean opt-in trusting ONLY this fleet's own configured GitHub App for gate-scoped secrets. Default false: OFF, the #1346 default -- every bot-authored PR (including this fleet's own App) is denied. When true, a PR is trusted on the app-bot path iff user.type == "Bot" AND user.login === "<slug>[bot]" EXACTLY (never a prefix/substring match), where <slug> is read fresh from GitHub's `GET /app` for THIS Worker's own configured App credentials -- never operator input -- on the repo's own default branch, same-repo. Every OTHER bot (dependabot etc) stays denied regardless; there is no slug list here for an operator to mistype into trusting the wrong App (an earlier free-form 'trustApps: string[]' design, plus an 'if available' App-id cross-check, was replaced after security review r1 found that cross-check dead -- the only JWT-authenticated endpoint available could only ever confirm this Worker's own App, never verify which App actually authored a PR). Threat model: this trusts EVERY studio-authored PR, including a prompt-injected one -- mitigation is staging-only rotatable credentials (same as every other grant in this file) plus the still-open egress-allowlist gap (https://github.com/rafarc21/fleetflare/issues/1355).

additionalProperties.description: Leg name -> that leg's grant, for this one repo.

oneOf.description: Back-compat array form: the secret NAMEs this leg may receive. Equivalent to {"secrets": [...]} with no head opt-in.

#1376: object form. 'head' opts this leg's own @head union-plan copy (the name a leg a PR ADDS to, or changes the command/image/timeout of, in its own fleet.json runs under -- fanout.ts's headLegName) into sharing this SAME grant, under the exact same trust filter -- never a looser one. Named 'bun' or 'vitest' specifically, the copy is @head-<n> instead (the auto-sharded bun-test/vitest lanes, literally named bun-<n>/vitest-<n> -- no other leg is ever auto-sharded). A PR cannot set this itself: like every other entry here, it lives only in the OPS repo.

secrets.description: Secret NAMEs (must exist in secrets-registry.ts's SECRET_REGISTRY; an unknown name grants nothing, and is logged).

head.description: Default false (unchanged #1346 behavior: no head grants). true: this leg's @head copy (@head-<n> only for a leg literally named 'bun' or 'vitest') gets the same grant as the base leg.
